claims.text: The trip ran 1.6 km off the recommended route: the platform's own recorded distances are 22.9 km actual against 21.3 km recommended (EV-TRIP-05011), 7.5 per cent over, and the trip record shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19 and rejoining at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road at 08:22:49. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so the two within-tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are unavailable on these facts, and the 19.158 km figure in the trace is not a distance measure — POL-RD-22 says the trace shows which route was taken and when, not how long it was.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record. POL-RD-23 permits a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure — an advisory that both intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The one advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-05011-01) is an ACCIDENT on the PIE and its window 07:44:37 to 08:54:37 does overlap the trip, but the artifact's own derived fields record intersects_route as null and justifies_reroute as null, with the express note that the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route. Nothing else in the record ties that accident to the carriageway the vehicle was on: the advisory's text tells traffic to 'Avoid lanes 1 and 2', it does not tell any vehicle to leave the expressway, and the driver's assertion is the only thing linking the incident to the route he took. A conjunctive requirement with one limb left undetermined is not satisfied, so row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refundable in full.

Even if the judge finds the reroute traffic-justified, the rider was not informed as POL-RD-21 requires — before or at the point of deviation. The deviation began at 08:12:19 (EV-TRIP-05011). The chat log is IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight 0.4, and I disclose that and do not present it as clean: MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19, 210 seconds apart and on opposite sides of the deviation event, so the device clock puts the notice before the deviation and the server clock puts it after. On the server timeline the driver's message reached the rider at 08:14:19 and the rider's reply at 08:14:39, minutes after the vehicle had already left the PIE, and the message is phrased in the past tense — 'I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?' — describing a reroute already taken. in_app_calls is empty, so there is no recorded verbal notice either. On that footing the rider was not informed and row (b) of POL-RD-24 applies; and if the judge finds the timing of notice cannot be established at all from a 0.4-weight log, the open question is held under POL-GEN-26 rather than the fare being kept.

The 'ok can' at 08:14:39 does not turn this into the agreed deviation of row (a). POL-RD-21's agreement limb operates on an acknowledgment of a deviation the driver has given notice of before or at the point of deviation; assent sent after the vehicle has already left the recommended route and is running down Dunearn Road is acquiescence to a reroute already in progress, not the timely notice the clause requires — the driver took the exit first and asked afterwards. That acknowledgment is also provable only from an artifact impaired at 0.4 for CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so it cannot carry the driver's case.

The money the matrix moves is the excess distance fare, without surge: the deviation distance of 1.60 km times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, which the fare ledger's own derived block already states as excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.15. The 1.3 surge multiplier and the 7.65 SGD surge amount carried on this metered fare are not applied to the excess distance, and rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both pay that excess distance fare in full.

I do not press the rider's claim for the whole 37.55 SGD fare. POL-RD-24's matrix never returns the whole trip fare — its refund rows return the excess distance fare — and the lateness the rider describes has no monetary remedy in this version, so asking for the full 37.55 back would be asking for a remedy the policy does not provide. The rider's case is put on the excess distance fare of 1.15 SGD, which is PARTIAL_REFUND in POL-GEN-03's vocabulary: part of the trip's charge returned, and the rider left not carrying the disputed excess.

claims.text: The route deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: 22.9 km actual against a 21.3 km recommended route is a deviation of 1.60 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. This case therefore turns on justification and on notice, not on tolerance — which is the ground the rider chose when she filed.

The reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is an LTA advisory of type ACCIDENT — an 'incident' in the policy's admissible traffic_justification_types — on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37 to 08:54:37, a window that contains the entire deviation (08:12:19 to 08:22:49), and the artifact records overlaps_trip_window as true. The trip record's own route_deviation_detected event states that at 08:12:19 the recommended route was the Pan-Island Expressway and the vehicle left it at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit, and EV-GPS-05011's fixes place the vehicle on the PIE immediately before that point. The advisory's stated road and direction are exactly the road and direction of the recommended route at the point of departure. The artifact leaves intersects_route and justifies_reroute null and marked 'determined_by: judge'; I ask the judge to determine them on the road, direction, location and validity window the advisory itself states, which the record corroborates.

The driver informed the rider before the point of deviation. MSG-05011-003 — 'Accident on PIE after Adam Rd, I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?' — carries a device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a read_at of 08:11:13, both before route_deviation_detected at 08:12:19, so the notice was given before the deviation as POL-RD-21 requires. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05011 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: that one entry carries a server delivered_at of 08:14:19, 210 s later and on the far side of the deviation event, and I do not present the log as clean. The impairment does not defeat the point: the read receipt at 08:11:13 is itself a server-side timestamp, and it cannot on the server's own clock precede the server's own delivery at 08:14:19 — the internally consistent reading of the entry, and the only one that reconciles with the receipt, is the earlier one.

The rider acknowledged the reroute on the record. MSG-05011-004 — 'ok can' — was sent 08:14:39, delivered 08:14:42 and read 08:14:49, all inside the deviation window, which ran from 08:12:19 until the vehicle rejoined at 08:22:49. Those three timestamps agree across the device and server sources within 3 s, as the admissibility notes record for every entry other than MSG-05011-003. POL-RD-21 provides in terms that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. The rider replied 'ok can' while the vehicle was on the deviated route and objected to nothing at the time; her later assertion that the driver 'did not ask me before turning' is contradicted by the message she read at 08:11:13 and answered at 08:14:39.

On POL-RD-24 this case fits row (a) and no other: the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed and agreed, and the deviation was over 1 km. Row (a) gives no refund. Under POL-GEN-03 that leaves the present state standing: the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the 37.55 SGD the rider paid stays with the driver and her claim is not supported.

Quite apart from the merits, the relief the rider asks for is not available on the matrix she has invoked. She disputes the whole 37.55 SGD fare, but no row of POL-RD-24 ever returns a trip fare; the only sum the deviation matrix moves is the excess distance fare, which on the recorded figures is 1.15 SGD (1.60 km at fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, no surge applied). Nor is her lateness for an appointment a head of loss the matrix compensates. A full-fare refund of 37.55 SGD therefore cannot be granted on any view of this evidence.

This case is one the AI may decide, and the confidence required is 0.80. Neither profile carries a fraud flag — the value on EV-RPROF-05011 and EV-DPROF-05011 is 0 — so under POL-GEN-22 the 0.95 threshold does not apply, and the contested value of 37.55 SGD falls in the 10.00 to 50.00 band that requires 0.80. POL-RD-25 adds nothing beyond that here, because its 2 km limb is not in force: ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false, so the 1.60 km deviation does not force escalation on that ground.

The deciding facts are not carried by impaired evidence alone. The notification and the acknowledgment are each carried by two artifacts: EV-CHAT-05011 at weight 0.4, and EV-TRIP-05011 at weight 1.0 — a separate, COMPLETE artifact whose derived messages_during_trip block records the same two messages, MSG-05011-003 at 08:10:49 and MSG-05011-004 at 08:14:39, against POL-RD-21. The deviation distance and the traffic justification rest on EV-TRIP-05011 and EV-ADVIS-05011-01, both at weight 1.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence is capped at the lowest multiplier among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and at the highest where two or more independent artifacts carry it; the judge determines whether the trip record's message block is independent of the chat log, and on the driver's case it is, so the cap is not 0.4.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case is escalated to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26. No refund and no charge moves; the contested SGD 37.55 is held.

What is established. Your trip ran 1.60 km off the recommended route — 22.9 km recorded against 21.3 km recommended on EV-TRIP-05011 — which is over the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22, so both advocates are right that the two within-tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 are unavailable. The vehicle left the PIE at the Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19 and rejoined at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road at 08:22:49.

Justification (POL-RD-23) — decided for the driver. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is an ACCIDENT, an 'incident' in the policy's admissible traffic-justification types, on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37 to 08:54:37, which overlaps the 08:12:19–08:22:49 deviation. The rider's point that the artifact leaves intersects_route and justifies_reroute null is noted, but those fields are expressly left for the judge to determine from the advisory's road, direction and location against the trip: the departure point at Eng Neo is on the same PIE towards-Changi carriageway and west of the Adam Road exit, so the incident lies on the recommended route the driver was on. The reroute was traffic-justified, and the rider's contrary claim (row (d)) is rejected.

What cannot be established is notice (POL-RD-21). The only carrier of whether the driver informed the rider before or at the point of deviation is EV-CHAT-05011, which is impaired at weight 0.4 for CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19, 210 s later and on the far side of the 08:12:19 deviation, and the admissibility note records that the device clock puts the notice before the deviation and the server clock after it. The driver's reading (that the 08:11:13 read receipt makes the earlier timeline the only consistent one) is one of the two the artifact holds; the record does not let me prefer it, because that contradiction is the very defect. EV-TRIP-05011's messages_during_trip block repeats the same messages and is not an independent carrier (POL-GEN-02(2)). An undecided limb supports neither row (a), which needs timely notice, nor row (b), which needs the rider to have been uninformed, so the case fits no row. The rider's 'ok can' at 08:14:39 has three agreeing timestamps, but it was sent after the vehicle had already left the PIE, so it cannot by itself make this a timely agreed deviation. The open question for the reviewer is therefore: was the driver's reroute message given to the rider before or at 08:12:19?

Confidence. The notice fact is carried only by EV-CHAT-05011 at weight 0.4, so the cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 0.4. POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-22 require 0.80 for a 37.55 SGD dispute with no fraud flags (the 2 km limb is not in force, ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false, as the driver correctly says), so the bar is not met and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation.

On the money, for completeness: had a refund been due it would be the excess distance fare only, 1.60 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD without surge (EV-FARE-05011), as both sides accept. The full 37.55 SGD the rider asks for is not available on any row of POL-RD-24, and no lateness remedy exists in this version. No sum issues on an escalation. No referral applies — POL-NS-24, POL-NS-25 and POL-NS-22 have no application to a route deviation.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the deviation itself is established. The platform's recorded distances are 22.9 km actual against 21.3 km recommended — 1.60 km (7.5%) off, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 — so this is not a within-tolerance case, and both advocates are right about that. It is also right that the only money the POL-RD-24 matrix can ever return is the excess distance fare, which on the recorded figures is 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, with no surge applied; no row of POL-RD-24 returns the whole 37.55 SGD fare the rider asked for, and the appointment lateness she describes has no monetary remedy in this version. So the most a refund could ever be here is 1.15 SGD.

What I cannot decide on this record is whether any refund or no-action row applies, because two facts POL-RD-24 needs are not established.

(1) Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is an ACCIDENT, an admissible incident type, on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37-08:54:37, which covers the deviation window 08:12:19-08:22:49. But the artifact itself records that the record does not say whether that advisory lies on the recommended route, and nothing else in the record fixes the recommended PIE segment as extending past the Adam Road exit before the route joins the CTE at the Bukit Timah Road slip road. The driver's assertion that the accident lay on his route is not enough where the traffic data do not establish it; equally, the advisory is not shown to be off the route, so the rider's 'not justified' case is not made out either. The intersection is genuinely open.

(2) Notice (POL-RD-21). Whether the driver told the rider before or at the point of deviation turns on the chat log EV-CHAT-05011, and that artifact is impaired at weight 0.4 on issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: MSG-05011-003 ('Accident on PIE after Adam Rd, I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?') carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 (before the deviation) and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19 (after it) — 210 s apart and on opposite sides of the deviation event, with the read receipt at 08:11:13 not reconciling the two clocks. The rider's 'ok can' at 08:14:39 came while the vehicle was already on Dunearn Road, so even the acknowledgment does not settle timely notice or agreement. The trip record's messages_during_trip block repeats the same two messages and is not an independent carrier, so it does not lift the cap.

Because the only artifact that can carry the notice timing sits at weight 0.4, my confidence is capped (POL-GEN-02(2)) at 0.40, below the 0.80 that POL-RD-25 requires and that POL-GEN-22 requires for a contested value of 37.55 SGD in the 10.00-50.00 band with no fraud flags (both profiles show fraud_flags 0). POL-GEN-26 requires escalation where a fact a rule needs cannot be established, and POL-GEN-22's band is reproduced in route_deviation.thresholds. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb does not add anything here, as ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false. I am therefore holding the 37.55 SGD charge rather than collecting or refunding it, and sending the file to a human reviewer. Open questions for the reviewer, not instructions: did the accident in EV-ADVIS-05011-01 lie on the recommended PIE segment at the trip time; and did MSG-05011-003 reach the rider before 08:12:19? No referral clause fires (no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit, no POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag, no POL-NS-22 fee-amount issue on this category).

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the shape of the trip, and so do I. The platform's own recorded distances are 22.9 km actual against a 21.3 km recommended route (EV-TRIP-05011) — a deviation of 1.60 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 — so the two "within tolerance" rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are unavailable. The 19.158 km trace figure is not a distance measure; POL-RD-22 uses the trace only to show which route was taken and when.

On traffic justification (POL-RD-23) I find the reroute WAS justified, so I reject the rider's argument that it was not. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is an LTA advisory of type ACCIDENT — an admissible "incident" type — on the Pan-Island Expressway towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37 to 08:54:37, a window that contains the whole deviation (08:12:19 to 08:22:49), and it records overlaps_trip_window as true. The artifact left intersects_route for the judge to determine. On its road (PIE, the recommended route's road), its direction (towards Changi, the vehicle's direction of travel) and its location (after Adam Road, on the stretch the vehicle would have continued along), it intersects the recommended route. The rider is right that the advisory orders no vehicle off the expressway, but POL-RD-23 requires only traffic data showing an incident on the recommended route segment at the trip time, which this is; and the null field is expressly marked for the judge, not a failed limb.

That leaves the notice limb of POL-RD-21, which decides between row (a) (informed and agreed — no refund) and row (b) (not informed — refund of the excess distance fare). That fact cannot be established on this record, and both advocates' timing claims fail on it. The notice is carried only by the chat log EV-CHAT-05011, which is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19 — 210 seconds apart, and on opposite sides of the 08:12:19 deviation event. I reject the driver's submission that the read receipt at 08:11:13 rescues the earlier reading: that timestamp sits before the server's own delivery time, so the three timestamps for that one message cannot all be true, and the conflict is real rather than a mere flag. I also reject the driver's submission that the trip record's message block (EV-TRIP-05011) independently carries the notice at weight 1.0: it repeats the same two messages from the same chat system and is a restatement of the same measurement, not a second carrier. The rider's "he did not ask me before turning" therefore cannot be resolved against the driver, and the driver's "I messaged the passenger before I exit" cannot be resolved for him; the account in the counterparty statement does not meet a limb POL-RD-21 ties to the chat log or a call recording.

Because the fact that decides between rows (a) and (b) rests on impaired evidence, POL-GEN-26 and POL-RD-24's "fits no row" rule send this to a human reviewer, and POL-RD-25 does the same: my confidence is capped by POL-GEN-02(2) at the 0.4 weight of the only artifact carrying the notice fact, below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 and POL-RD-25 require for a route-deviation ruling at this value. The contested 37.55 SGD sits in the 10.00–50.00 SGD band; neither profile carries a fraud flag (both read 0), so the 0.95 threshold does not apply.

No money issues. The disputed 37.55 SGD is held — not refunded, not kept. For completeness, I accept, as the driver does, that the only sum the matrix ever moves is the excess distance fare of 1.15 SGD (1.60 km at the 0.72 SGD per-km rate, without the 1.3 surge), which is what the rider now asks and what the driver correctly says no row can exceed; the full 37.55 SGD fare and the rider's lateness for her appointment are not remedies POL-RD-24 provides. But that figure cannot be paid at 0.4 confidence.

Open question for the human reviewer: from the driver's device clock the notice came before the deviation, from the platform's server clock it came after. The reviewer should determine which clock is right, and whether the rider's "ok can" at 08:14:39 was agreement to a notice already given or acquiescence to a reroute already under way.

ledger.claim: The trip ran 1.6 km off the recommended route: the platform's own recorded distances are 22.9 km actual against 21.3 km recommended (EV-TRIP-05011), 7.5 per cent over, and the trip record shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19 and rejoining at the Bukit Timah Road / CTE slip road at 08:22:49. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so the two within-tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are unavailable on these facts, and the 19.158 km figure in the trace is not a distance measure — POL-RD-22 says the trace shows which route was taken and when, not how long it was.

The reroute is not traffic-justified on this record. POL-RD-23 permits a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure — an advisory that both intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The one advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-05011-01) is an ACCIDENT on the PIE and its window 07:44:37 to 08:54:37 does overlap the trip, but the artifact's own derived fields record intersects_route as null and justifies_reroute as null, with the express note that the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route. Nothing else in the record ties that accident to the carriageway the vehicle was on: the advisory's text tells traffic to 'Avoid lanes 1 and 2', it does not tell any vehicle to leave the expressway, and the driver's assertion is the only thing linking the incident to the route he took. A conjunctive requirement with one limb left undetermined is not satisfied, so row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refundable in full.

Even if the judge finds the reroute traffic-justified, the rider was not informed as POL-RD-21 requires — before or at the point of deviation. The deviation began at 08:12:19 (EV-TRIP-05011). The chat log is IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight 0.4, and I disclose that and do not present it as clean: MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19, 210 seconds apart and on opposite sides of the deviation event, so the device clock puts the notice before the deviation and the server clock puts it after. On the server timeline the driver's message reached the rider at 08:14:19 and the rider's reply at 08:14:39, minutes after the vehicle had already left the PIE, and the message is phrased in the past tense — 'I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?' — describing a reroute already taken. in_app_calls is empty, so there is no recorded verbal notice either. On that footing the rider was not informed and row (b) of POL-RD-24 applies; and if the judge finds the timing of notice cannot be established at all from a 0.4-weight log, the open question is held under POL-GEN-26 rather than the fare being kept.

The 'ok can' at 08:14:39 does not turn this into the agreed deviation of row (a). POL-RD-21's agreement limb operates on an acknowledgment of a deviation the driver has given notice of before or at the point of deviation; assent sent after the vehicle has already left the recommended route and is running down Dunearn Road is acquiescence to a reroute already in progress, not the timely notice the clause requires — the driver took the exit first and asked afterwards. That acknowledgment is also provable only from an artifact impaired at 0.4 for CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so it cannot carry the driver's case.

POL-RD-24's matrix never returns the whole trip fare — its refund rows return the excess distance fare — and the lateness the rider describes has no monetary remedy in this version, so asking for the full 37.55 back would be asking for a remedy the policy does not provide. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence is capped at the lowest multiplier among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and at the highest where two or more independent artifacts carry it; the judge determines whether the trip record's message block is independent of the chat log, and on the driver's case it is, so the cap is not 0.4.
